sources.title: SUMCO: Production Processes
sources.support: CZ uses an oriented seed and melt; wafer forming separates slicing, lapping, damage-removal etch, polishing and inspection. Epitaxy adds crystalline film.
sources.scopeLimit: Supplier overview; no tolerances, complete purification chemistry or production recipe is adopted.

sources.title: ASM: Epitaxy
sources.support: Identifies Si/SiGe/Si:P films, crystal/strain roles, selective growth and prepared surface requirements.
sources.scopeLimit: No layer recipe, defect prediction, strain limit or guaranteed material selectivity is adopted.

sources.title: ASM: Atomic Layer Deposition
sources.support: Separated exposures and purges support saturated surface reactions and cycle-controlled films.
sources.scopeLimit: A schematic cycle does not promise one complete atomic plane, complete saturation in all features or a universal growth rate.

sources.title: Lam Research: Deposition
sources.support: CVD/ALD and physical deposition supply different films and applications.
sources.scopeLimit: Not a quantitative predictor of profile, chemistry or coverage.

sources.title: Lam Research: Etch
sources.support: Material removal can be directional or selective, with process-specific geometry.
sources.scopeLimit: Do not label every plasma etch anisotropic or every wet etch isotropic.

sources.title: Lam Research: Strip & Clean
sources.support: Strip/clean are separate surface-preparation and residue-removal operations.
sources.scopeLimit: Clean appearance and particle reduction alone do not establish chemistry, damage or readiness.

sources.title: Entegris: Understanding AMC
sources.support: Gas-phase molecular contamination differs from particles and requires species-relevant measurement.
sources.scopeLimit: No contamination acceptance level or relation between ambient exposure and deposited dose is inferred.

sources.title: Deal and Grove: General Relationship for the Thermal Oxidation of Silicon
sources.support: Oxidation couples oxidant transport and interfacial reaction; x²+Ax=B(t+tau) is a bounded model.
sources.scopeLimit: University-hosted excerpt of the original paper; complete experimental results are not reproduced. No recipe coefficients adopted.

sources.title: ASML: Six crucial steps in semiconductor manufacturing
sources.support: Exposure changes resist solubility and positive/negative tones retain different regions.
sources.scopeLimit: Use only these named sections. The overview blurs develop and etch in its Etch paragraph; this asset keeps them separate. No purity or current product metrics adopted.

sources.title: ASML: Computational lithography
sources.support: Calibrated process models modify mask patterns to improve the printed target.
sources.scopeLimit: Our geometric toy uses prescribed contours; it is not ASML OPC, an optical field solver or a qualified mask.

sources.title: ASML: Lenses & mirrors
sources.support: DUV lenses and EUV mirrors are distinct; numerical aperture participates in resolution scaling.
sources.scopeLimit: No universal process window, exact scanner architecture or current product availability is inferred.

sources.title: MIT 6.152J: Micro/Nano Processing Technology
sources.support: Existing atlas foundation reference for oxidation, CVD/PVD, lithography and wet/dry etch.
sources.scopeLimit: Index page checked; not cited as freshly revalidated lecture-detail evidence.

sources.title: Samsung: HBM3E 12H announcement
sources.support: Confirms the thermocompression/non-conductive-film route and metal bumps between dies.
sources.scopeLimit: Dated supplier product announcement; its gap, thermal and performance figures are not adopted as simulation inputs or universal bounds.

sources.title: SK hynix: Small Size, Big Impact
sources.support: MR forms metallic joints; MUF fills inter-die/external regions. Advanced variants can stabilize dies during placement before final reflow.
sources.scopeLimit: Supplier route overview. Do not infer exact alloy from informal wording, a proprietary thermal profile, zero pre-reflow bonding or a universal productivity gain.

sources.title: imec: Wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding
sources.support: Local Cu/dielectric preparation, CMP, alignment/contact, then anneal are distinct. Electrical test structures have a stated population.
sources.scopeLimit: W2W research vehicle, not a shipping HBM process. Numeric pitch/recess/overlay/yield results must not become HBM pass limits.

sources.title: imec: Die-to-wafer hybrid bonding demonstration
sources.support: D2W must preserve surface quality through singulation and placement; test structures establish limited electrical evidence.
sources.scopeLimit: D2W research is distinct from W2W; no demonstrated vehicle metric is transferred to a complete HBM product.

steps.title: Conditioned resist before exposure
steps.transform: Pre-exposure conditioning changes the resist’s state while its schematic geometry remains continuous. The chemistry-dependent conditioning step does not require a visible thickness change in this representation.

measurement.question: Which recorded conditioning stage applies?
measurement.scopeLimit: Do not force a visible shrinkage or universal bake recipe.

steps.title: A latent chemical image
steps.transform: Exposure identifies regions of this positive resist that become more soluble after the applicable processing. The latent image changes chemistry; it has not yet removed resist or etched the target film.

measurement.question: Where did the resist chemistry change?
measurement.scopeLimit: No photoresist removal during exposure.
measurement.dataStatus: measurement to explain; numerical traces, if supplied, are synthetic unless separately sourced

steps.title: An opening in the resist
steps.transform: Development removes the selected soluble resist and leaves a relief pattern. The target film beneath the opening remains intact until a separate pattern-transfer operation.

measurement.question: What CD/profile exists after develop?
measurement.scopeLimit: Development is not target-film etching.

steps.title: Development and etch measurements
steps.input: Developed resist and separately identified etched sample
steps.transform: The primary cross-section remains in the developed state. A separate synthetic comparison pairs a 24 nm after-develop dimension with a 21 nm after-etch dimension, giving a −3 nm transfer bias without identifying its cause.

measurement.question: What does the measured bias establish?
measurement.scopeLimit: Bias does not identify etch cause or electrical width.

routes.name: Target, corrected mask and predicted contour
routes.scientificScope: A geometry/optimization explanation with supplied synthetic wafer contours. Top-down target/mask/image views are primary; a 3D context locates the same reticle and wafer field. No full imaging/OPC solver.

steps.title: The desired wafer pattern
steps.transform: The target defines the intended wafer geometry. Its lane is separate from the mask lane; their apparent sizes do not imply a physical reticle-to-wafer magnification.

measurement.question: Which contour is the target?
measurement.scopeLimit: Normalize mask/wafer coordinates explicitly.
measurement.dataStatus: measurement to explain; numerical traces, if supplied, are synthetic unless separately sourced

steps.title: An initial mask candidate
steps.transform: The initial mask provides a pattern intended to produce the wafer target. Similarity between those two drawings alone does not establish the wafer image after optical and resist effects.

measurement.question: How does mask geometry differ from wafer coordinates?
measurement.scopeLimit: Reticle magnification is not implied by visual size.
measurement.dataStatus: measurement to explain; numerical traces, if supplied, are synthetic unless separately sourced

steps.title: A prescribed uncorrected contour
steps.transform: The synthetic wafer contour differs from the target edges. The supplied edge values give a squared error of 8 nm²; the contour is a constructed example rather than an optical calculation or wafer measurement.

measurement.question: Which errors change with local pattern context?
measurement.scopeLimit: A supplied contour is not a measured wafer.

steps.title: A corrected mask candidate
steps.transform: The candidate mask includes local edge and corner adjustments. Such mask changes can compensate imaging effects, but this example does not predict which features print or solve an OPC optimization.

measurement.question: What is changed on the mask?
measurement.scopeLimit: Do not automatically print every assist feature.

steps.title: The prescribed corrected contour
steps.transform: The supplied corrected contour reduces the squared edge error to 0.5 nm² for this example. That improvement belongs to the stated synthetic contours and does not establish a dose, focus, or process window.

measurement.question: Is improvement shared by all contexts?
measurement.scopeLimit: No invented optical dose/focus model.

steps.title: Validation beyond the contour example
steps.transform: The target, candidate mask, and prescribed wafer contour remain separate. Production use would require calibrated imaging behavior, mask inspection, and wafer evidence beyond this geometric comparison.

measurement.question: What evidence would validate the model?
measurement.scopeLimit: No full-chip or production-ready claim.

routes.name: Finite aperture and focus scaling
routes.scientificScope: Optical scaling comparison, not a scanner model. Separate ray/image schematic from actual spatial wafer section. DUV and EUV optical classes are distinct; presets are not node labels or shipping claims.

steps.title: An abstract imaging boundary
steps.transform: The source-to-image schematic locates an optical boundary and an image plane. It is neither a DUV lens assembly nor an EUV mirror prescription, and it carries no marketed node dimension.

measurement.question: Which variables define the optical model?
measurement.scopeLimit: Do not use marketed node name as dimension.
measurement.dataStatus: measurement to explain; numerical traces, if supplied, are synthetic unless separately sourced

steps.title: A finite numerical aperture
steps.transform: The aperture marker represents the finite range of accepted light directions. Relative numerical aperture controls the stated scaling bounds; the schematic does not solve the optical field.

measurement.question: What changes when NA increases?
measurement.scopeLimit: Schematic angular cone is not full vector imaging.
measurement.dataStatus: measurement to explain; numerical traces, if supplied, are synthetic unless separately sourced

steps.title: Relative resolution scaling
steps.transform: With wavelength and process coefficients fixed, the relative resolution bound varies inversely with numerical aperture. The bound is not a prediction of the developed resist profile or final device dimension.

measurement.question: How does resolution scale under fixed assumptions?
measurement.scopeLimit: Actual k1/process effects omitted.
measurement.dataStatus: measurement to explain; numerical traces, if supplied, are synthetic unless separately sourced

steps.title: Relative depth-of-focus scaling
steps.transform: Under the same fixed assumptions, relative depth of focus varies inversely with numerical aperture squared. The marked focus range illustrates this scaling without certifying a usable resist process window.

measurement.question: Why does DOF change faster than resolution?
measurement.scopeLimit: Envelope does not certify resist process window.
measurement.dataStatus: measurement to explain; numerical traces, if supplied, are synthetic unless separately sourced

steps.title: After-develop evidence
steps.transform: The optical geometry stays fixed while critical dimension, roughness, and defect measurements address the resist result. Numerical aperture alone cannot establish acceptable patterning across focus and exposure.

measurement.question: Which measurements go beyond optical bounds?
measurement.scopeLimit: Cannot infer accepted geometry from NA alone.

steps.title: Evidence after pattern transfer
steps.transform: Transferred dimensions and alignment require evidence beyond the optical bounds. The unchanged aperture schematic does not establish etch bias, overlay performance, or the final transistor geometry.

measurement.question: What has been checked at which stage?
measurement.scopeLimit: Optical bound does not establish final transistor dimension.

routes.name: Target removal, mask loss and profile
routes.scientificScope: A representative directional target-removal cross-section with an explicit finite-mask thickness budget. Plasma and wet etch can have process-specific profiles; this view does not model an isotropic wet-etch case.

steps.title: Mask and exposed target
steps.transform: The developed mask separates protected and exposed target regions before removal begins. The initial 40 nm mask is a finite material budget, not an infinitely durable boundary.

measurement.question: Which material is target and which is protected?
measurement.scopeLimit: Positive resist development has already occurred.
measurement.dataStatus: measurement to explain; numerical traces, if supplied, are synthetic unless separately sourced

steps.title: Initial target and mask removal
steps.transform: The first illustrative removal stage consumes both exposed target and some mask. Selectivity relates their removed thicknesses without simulating reaction kinetics, transport, or profile evolution.

measurement.question: What makes this profile case directional or lateral?
measurement.scopeLimit: Arrows do not solve transport or crystal etch rates.
measurement.dataStatus: measurement to explain; numerical traces, if supplied, are synthetic unless separately sourced

steps.title: A partially transferred profile
steps.transform: The requested target depth reaches 100 nm, with mask loss calculated as depth divided by selectivity. The geometry is conditional on the thickness budget and does not establish a universal linear etch rate.

measurement.question: How much mask budget remains?
measurement.scopeLimit: No universal linear profile kinetics.
measurement.dataStatus: measurement to explain; numerical traces, if supplied, are synthetic unless separately sourced

steps.title: Requested depth and mask budget
steps.transform: At the illustrative 200 nm target depth, selectivity determines the calculated remaining mask. An exhausted budget makes the requested profile unqualified; nonuniformity and overetch allowances are outside this simple calculation.

measurement.question: Would the starting mask leave any margin?
measurement.scopeLimit: No overetch/nonuniformity allowance in simple equation.
measurement.dataStatus: measurement to explain; numerical traces, if supplied, are synthetic unless separately sourced

steps.title: Inspection after transfer
steps.transform: The etched geometry stays fixed while synthetic markers identify locations for inspection. Residue, profile, and damage require separate evidence; a marker does not establish a damage mechanism or cleaning recipe.

measurement.question: Are depth, profile, residue and damage all acceptable for the next step?
measurement.scopeLimit: No modeled damage mechanism or automatic clean recipe.

steps.title: Transferred geometry and remaining mask
steps.transform: The final profile and its remaining mask describe different outcomes of transfer. A dimensional change between development and etching would still need matched measurements and further evidence to establish a cause.

measurement.question: What changed between resist and target material?
measurement.scopeLimit: AE-AD alone does not establish a root cause.
